questions.stem: What does 「しゅうしょく」 mean?
options: Moving from one job to another job
Starting work after finishing study
Going on to the next stage of study
Retiring from work at the end of a career
questions.explanation: 「しゅうしょく」 is finding and starting a job, often straight after school or university. Going on to further study is 「しんがく」, changing jobs is 「てんしょく」 and retiring is 「たいしょく」: similar sounds for different steps in a working life.

questions.stem: What does 「しんろ」 mean in a talk with a careers teacher?
options: The path a student takes after leaving school
The timetable of subjects for the final year of school
The entrance exam for one particular university
A part-time job taken during the school holidays
questions.explanation: 「しんろ」 is one's course after school, so 「しんろについて先生と話す」 is a careers conversation about university, training or work. An entrance exam is 「にゅうし」, one step on that path rather than the path itself.

questions.stem: What does 「せいしゃいん」 mean?
options: A student doing work experience
A permanent full-time employee
A casual worker paid by the hour
The president of a company
questions.explanation: 「せいしゃいん」 are a company's regular staff, employed full time with no fixed end date. Casual hourly work is 「アルバイト」 or 「パート」, and the company president is 「社長」.

questions.stem: 「日本では、大学四年生の多くが、そつぎょうする前にしゅうしょく活動をします。」 What does the sentence say?
options: Many students take a part-time job in their fourth year
Many fourth-year students look for work before they graduate
Many students begin looking for work only after they graduate
Many fourth-year students take a year off before starting work
questions.explanation: 「しゅうしょく活動」 is job hunting, and 「そつぎょうする前に」 places it before graduation. A part-time job would be 「アルバイト」, which is not a search for a career.

questions.stem: What does 「自分らしく生きたい。」 mean?
options: I want to live in a way that is true to myself
It seems that I want to live on my own
I want to live the way that everyone else does
I want to live somewhere close to my family
questions.explanation: After a noun, 〜らしい means typical of or true to, so 「自分らしく」 is 'in a way that is true to myself'. After a plain-form verb or clause, らしい means 'apparently', which is the trap behind the 'it seems' reading.

questions.stem: What does 「生きがい」 mean?
options: The way a person earns a living
A healthy and balanced daily routine
Something that makes life feel worth living
The total number of years that a person lives
questions.explanation: 〜がい after a verb stem is the worth of doing something, so 「生きがい」 is what gives a life meaning, such as work, family or a hobby. The length of a life is 「じゅみょう」, a different word.

questions.stem: What does 「ともばたらき」 mean?
options: One partner works while the other stays at home
One person works two jobs at the same time
Both partners in a couple go out to work
Two people work together in the same company
questions.explanation: 「ともばたらき」 describes a household in which both partners have jobs. A household where one partner stays at home full time is the opposite situation, often discussed alongside it in articles on family life.

questions.stem: What does 「いくじきゅうか」 mean?
options: Leave from work to care for an elderly parent
Leave from work to care for a young child
Paid annual holiday leave from work
Leave from work while recovering from illness
questions.explanation: 「いくじ」 is raising a child and 「きゅうか」 is leave, so this is parental leave, often shortened to 「いくきゅう」. Leave to care for an elderly relative is 「かいごきゅうか」.

questions.stem: What does 「男女びょうどう」 mean?
options: The roles once expected of each sex
Equality between men and women
The ratio of men to women in a group
A school for both boys and girls
questions.explanation: 「びょうどう」 is equality, so 「男女びょうどう」 is gender equality, a key term in discussions of men and women in the workforce. A co-educational school is 「きょうがく」.

questions.stem: 「むかしは、けっこんしたら仕事をやめるじょせいが多かったが、今は子どもが生まれても働きつづける人がふえている。」 What change does the sentence describe?
options: More women now leave work when they marry than in the past
In the past most women kept working until their first child
Fewer women now marry, so more of them keep working
More women now keep working after having children
questions.explanation: The 「むかしは…が、今は…」 frame contrasts past and present: once many women left work when they married, and now more keep working even after a child is born. 「〜ても」 means even if, and 〜つづける means to keep doing.

questions.stem: What does 「長時間ろうどう」 mean?
options: Working part-time for many years
Working very long hours
A long daily commute to work
Staying at one company for decades
questions.explanation: 「長時間」 is long hours and 「ろうどう」 is labour, so the term names overwork. Staying with one employer for a whole career is 「しゅうしんこよう」, lifetime employment.

questions.stem: What is 「しゅうしんこよう」?
options: A rule that all employees must retire at a fixed age
The practice of staying with one employer from graduation to retirement
The practice of changing employers every few years to gain experience
A system in which every employee is paid by the hour
questions.explanation: 「しゅうしんこよう」 is lifetime employment: a graduate joins a company and stays for a whole career. It is the traditional model in many large Japanese companies and is often contrasted with changing jobs, 「てんしょく」.

questions.stem: 「しょうらいは、人のやくに立つ仕事がしたいです。」 What kind of work does the speaker want?
options: Work where they can stand up all day
Work that pays more than other jobs
Work at a large, well-known company
Work that is useful to other people
questions.explanation: 「やくに立つ」 is an expression meaning to be useful, so 「人のやくに立つ仕事」 is work that helps others. 「立つ」 on its own means to stand, which is the literal trap.

questions.stem: 「大学をそつぎょうしたら、一年ぐらい外国で働いてみるつもりです。」 What does the speaker say?
options: After graduating, I plan to try working abroad for about a year
Before university, I worked overseas for about a year
I will graduate after working overseas for about a year
After graduating, I may be required to work abroad for about a year
questions.explanation: 「〜たら」 puts graduation first, 「働いてみる」 is to try working, and 「つもりです」 states an intention. 'May have to' would need 「〜なければならないかもしれません」, which expresses obligation rather than a plan.

questions.stem: Which word completes 「日本の会社で働ける___、毎日日本語を勉強しています。」 ('I study Japanese every day so that I can work for a Japanese company')?
options: のに
から
ように
ために
questions.explanation: With a potential form such as 「働ける」, purpose is expressed with 〜ように. 〜ために needs a verb the speaker controls directly, as in 「日本の会社で働くために」, and 「のに」 means although.

questions.stem: 「父は、私が日本にりゅうがくすることにはんたいではありませんが、少ししんぱいしているようです。」 What does the speaker say about her father?
options: He would like to go to Japan with her while she studies
He does not oppose her studying in Japan but seems a little worried
He is against her studying in Japan and has told her so
He is worried that she will not be accepted to study in Japan
questions.explanation: 「はんたいではありません」 says he is not against it, and 「〜ようです」 marks the speaker's impression that he is worried. The sentence never says he has told her anything, so the second reading adds a fact.

questions.stem: In a Japanese school club, who is a 「せんぱい」?
options: A student in a lower year, who is helped and guided
The captain chosen by the club's members
A student in a higher year, who is shown respect
The teacher who supervises the club
questions.explanation: 「せんぱい」 are senior students and 「こうはい」 are juniors: juniors speak politely to their せんぱい, who in turn look after them. The supervising teacher is 「こもん」.

questions.stem: What does 「なかなおりする」 mean?
options: To become close friends with someone
To have an argument
To say sorry to someone
To make up after a quarrel
questions.explanation: 「なかなおり」 is mending a relationship, so it comes after 「けんかする」, to quarrel. Apologising, 「あやまる」, is often part of making up but is a separate verb.

questions.stem: What does 「しんゆう」 mean?
options: A close friend
A relative
A new acquaintance
A classmate
questions.explanation: 「しんゆう」 is a close or best friend. A relative is 「しんせき」, which shares the sound しん but not the meaning.

questions.stem: Which word completes 「ゆうきくんはやさしい___、おもしろいので、みんなに好かれています。」 ('Yuki is kind and funny, so everyone likes him')?
options: が
のに
ても
し
questions.explanation: Plain form + し lists reasons, 'and what's more', which then lead into 「ので」. 「のに」 (although), 「ても」 (even if) and 「が」 (but) all set up a contrast, but kind and funny are two points in the same direction.

questions.stem: 「先生に本をかしていただきました。」 What happened?
options: The speaker asked the teacher to buy a book
The teacher lent the speaker a book
The speaker lent the teacher a book
The teacher borrowed a book from the speaker
questions.explanation: 〜ていただく is the humble form of 〜てもらう: the speaker receives a favour from a superior, who is marked by に. 「かす」 is to lend, so the teacher did the lending; the reverse would be 「先生に本をおかししました」.

questions.stem: 「兄は大きな会社に入ったが、三年でやめて、今は小さな店をやっている。きゅうりょうは前より少ないらしいが、毎日楽しそうだ。」 What does the writer suggest about her brother?
options: He earns more than before and seems happier
He regrets leaving the large company
He works in a shop owned by his old company
He earns less than before but seems happier
questions.explanation: 「らしい」 marks the lower pay as something the writer has heard, and 「楽しそうだ」 is how he looks to her. The 「が」 sets the two side by side, so she suggests the change has been good for him despite the pay.

questions.stem: 「田中さんは来年、東京の大学に行くそうです。」 What does the sentence mean?
options: Tanaka looks as if he will go to a university in Tokyo next year
Tanaka wants to go to a university in Tokyo next year
Tanaka went to a university in Tokyo last year
I hear Tanaka is going to a university in Tokyo next year
questions.explanation: Plain form + そうです reports hearsay, 'I hear that'. The 'looks as if' meaning uses the verb stem, as in 「行きそうです」, so the form before そう decides the meaning.

questions.stem: What does 「ゆめをかなえる」 mean?
options: To give up on a dream
To describe a dream to others
To make a dream come true
To have a dream while asleep
questions.explanation: 「かなえる」 is to fulfil, so 「ゆめをかなえる」 is to realise an ambition; the intransitive 「ゆめがかなう」 is 'a dream comes true'. Giving up on a dream is 「ゆめをあきらめる」.

questions.stem: In a role-play with your host mother about coming home late, which reply acknowledges her view before you give your own?
options: おっしゃることはよくわかります。でも、土曜日だけは少しおそくてもいいですか。
それはちがうと思います。土曜日はもっとおそくまで外にいたいです。
どうしてだめなんですか。友だちはみんな十時まで外にいますよ。
土曜日はおそくなってもいいですよね。もう高校生ですから。
questions.explanation: 「おっしゃることはよくわかります」 shows you have heard and respect her concern, and 「でも」 then introduces your request politely. Appealing to what friends are allowed to do challenges her rule without acknowledging it.

questions.stem: In a role-play about coming home late, which sentence offers a compromise?
options: 九時に帰らなければならないのは、ちょっと早すぎると思います。
じゃあ、学校がある日は九時までに帰るので、土曜日だけ十時まででもいいですか。
土曜日はどうしても十時まで友だちといっしょにいたいんです。
みんなは十時まで外にいてもいいと言われているそうです。
questions.explanation: The speaker gives something up, home by nine on school days, in return for a later time on Saturday, which is the shape of a compromise. Insisting with 「どうしても」 only restates the request.

questions.stem: Which sentence confirms an agreed outcome at the end of a negotiation?
options: そうじはあまり好きじゃないんですが、どうしましょうか。
土曜日はアルバイトがあるかもしれないんです。
では、土曜日のそうじは私がするということで、いいですか。
土曜日のそうじについては、来週もう少し話しあってみませんか。
questions.explanation: 「では、〜ということで、いいですか」 sums up what has been agreed and asks the other speaker to confirm it. Suggesting more discussion with 「もう少し話しあってみませんか」 keeps the issue open.

questions.stem: Which sentence revisits an issue that has not yet been resolved?
options: はじめに、アルバイトについて話してもいいですか。
すみません、さっきのアルバイトの話にもどってもいいですか。
では、アルバイトは週に二回ということできまりですね。
アルバイトのことを聞いてくださって、ありがとうございます。
questions.explanation: 「さっきの〜の話にもどる」 is to go back to a point raised earlier, a polite way to reopen it. 「はじめに」 introduces a first topic, so it starts a discussion rather than returning to one.

questions.stem: 「ゲームの時間をへらすかわりに、しゅうまつに友だちと出かけてもいいですか。」 What is the speaker proposing?
options: To play more games instead of going out with friends at the weekend
To go out with friends instead of studying at the weekend
To play games with friends at the weekend instead of at home
To game less in return for going out with friends at the weekend
questions.explanation: 「〜かわりに」 here means 'in exchange for': the speaker offers to cut gaming time and asks for an outing in return. Reading かわりに only as 'instead of' swaps the roles of the two activities.

questions.stem: Which is the most appropriate way to ask your homestay father to drive you to the station?
options: 駅まで車でおくってもらいましたか。
駅まで車でおくっていただけませんか。
ねえ、駅まで車でおくってくれる？
よかったら、駅まで車でおくってあげましょうか。
questions.explanation: 〜ていただけませんか is a polite request for a favour from someone older. 「おくってあげましょうか」 offers to do the favour for him, which reverses who is helping whom, and 「おくってくれる？」 is too casual for this request.

questions.stem: A friend's mother invites you to stay for dinner, but you need to go home. Which reply declines politely?
options: ありがとう。でも、晩ごはんはいらない。
ありがとうございます。せっかくですが、今日はちょっと…。
いいえ、けっこうです。あまり食べたくないので、もう帰ります。
はい、ありがとうございます。いただきます。
questions.explanation: 「せっかくですが」 thanks her for the kind thought, and trailing off with 「ちょっと…」 declines without a blunt no. Saying you do not want to eat gives a reason that could offend.

questions.stem: When someone answers an invitation with 「その日はちょっと…。」, what do they usually mean?
options: They will come but may arrive a little late
They agree but would like more details first
They are declining without saying no directly
They did not hear the invitation clearly
questions.explanation: Leaving the sentence unfinished after 「ちょっと」 is a common indirect refusal: the listener understands 'that day is difficult' without hearing a direct いいえ. The softness protects the relationship.

questions.stem: In a negotiation, the other speaker replies 「考えておきます。」 to your request. What does this often signal?
options: A firm promise to give a final answer by the next day
Enthusiastic agreement to the request exactly as it stands
A request for all of the details to be put in writing
A polite way of avoiding an immediate yes, often a gentle no
questions.explanation: 「考えておきます」 literally promises to think it over, but because Japanese often avoids a direct refusal it frequently means no. Context and tone decide, so a good negotiator may follow up with a new offer.

questions.stem: In a discussion, what is 「たしかにそうですね。でも、」 used for?
options: Rejecting the other speaker's point outright
Conceding a point while keeping your own position
Agreeing completely and bringing the discussion to an end
Asking the other speaker to repeat their point
questions.explanation: 「たしかに」 (certainly) concedes that the other speaker has a point, and 「でも」 signals that a reservation follows. Conceding before qualifying keeps a negotiation cooperative.

questions.stem: What is 「つまり、〜ということですか。」 used for?
options: Changing the subject to a completely new point
Checking that you have understood the other speaker
Telling the other speaker politely that they are wrong
Asking the other speaker to speak more slowly
questions.explanation: 「つまり」 (in other words) restates what you think the other person meant, and 「〜ということですか」 asks them to confirm or correct it. Clarifying before responding keeps the exchange on track.

questions.stem: 「A『来月の旅行、一人で行きたいんだけど。』B『一人はちょっとしんぱいだな。』A『じゃあ、毎晩電話するってやくそくしたら、どう？』」 What is A doing in the last line?
options: Inviting B to come along on the trip with A
Complaining that B worries too much
Offering a condition to ease B's worry
Agreeing not to go on the trip at all
questions.explanation: 「〜たら、どう？」 proposes something, and the promise to ring every night answers B's concern directly. A neither gives up the trip nor criticises B, so this is a compromise move.

questions.stem: You need more time for an assignment. Which request to your teacher is appropriate?
options: 先生、しめきりを一日のばしてあげてもいいですか。
先生、しめきりを一日のばさなければなりません。
先生、しめきりを一日のばしていただけないでしょうか。
先生、しめきりを一日のばしてくれない？
questions.explanation: 〜ていただけないでしょうか is one of the most polite request forms, suited to a teacher. 「のばしてあげてもいいですか」 offers to do the teacher a favour, and 「のばさなければなりません」 announces an obligation rather than asking.

questions.stem: 「アルバイトをしてもいいけど、せいせきが下がらないようにしてね。」 What condition does the parent set?
options: You may work part-time as long as your grades do not drop
You must work part-time to help pay for your own schooling
You may work part-time once your grades have improved
You may not work part-time until the exams are over
questions.explanation: 「〜てもいい」 gives permission and 「〜ないようにしてね」 asks the child to make sure something does not happen. The permission is already given, so it does not depend on grades improving first.

questions.stem: 「月曜日から金曜日までは、十時すぎにゲームをしてはいけません。」 What is the rule?
options: No gaming at all from Monday to Friday
No gaming after ten o'clock from Monday to Friday
Gaming is allowed until ten o'clock on weekends only
Gaming is allowed after ten o'clock on weekdays
questions.explanation: 「〜てはいけません」 forbids something, and 「十時すぎに」 limits the rule to after ten. Nothing is said about earlier in the evening, so gaming before ten is not banned.

questions.stem: A senior student in your club asks you to help at Saturday's practice, but you are going out with your family that day. Which reply declines politely and offers an alternative?
options: はい、わかりました。家族とのよていはやめます。
すみません、土曜日は家族と出かけるんです。日曜日ならてつだえますが…。
土曜日は家族と出かけるので、ぜったいにむりです。ほかの人にたのんでください。
家族と出かけるので、てつだいたくありません。
questions.explanation: The apology, the explanatory 〜んです and the trailing 「が…」 soften the refusal, and 「日曜日なら」 offers another day. 「ぜったいにむりです」 followed by an instruction to ask someone else is too blunt to say to a せんぱい.
